findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed handwashing to occur in triple sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed at hand sink. Ensure hand washing is done solely at hand sinks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed cooked burgers to be hot holding in crock pot at 125F. Discussed with PIC, crockpot was placed on a warmer setting. Burgers are cooked on grill then moved to crock pot for hot holding. Inspector later observed hot holding tempatures of 145F. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed 2 bottles of sanitizer to be resting on the same shelf as TCS food items. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper chemical storage locations and sanitizer bottles were relocated. Ensure all chemicals are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no allergen training to be present for all CFM’s. Discussed with PIC, CFM’s will complete the required allergen training. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training and the correct documention is available during all hours of operation. 


410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice machine to have a build up of bacteria/mold to be present. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning ice machine at a frequency that prevents build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available for the facility. Facility has misplaced the folder (paperwork was present during last few routine inspections). Provided copy for the facility. Ensure all staff read and sign the document (including bar staff). Ensure new hires read and sign the documents as a part of onboarding. Keep copies of the paperwork in a public health folder or binder. Inspector will follow-up on 4/1/24.

Inspector is leaving SCDPH on 3/29/24. Inspector instructed PIC to text AS photos of the signed employee health reporting agreements next week before 3/29 to put a Spot Check in CDP and close out the violation. Cell: 217-891-3012.
